_note: 'Can I carry it on a flight?' (baggage/can-i-carry.html). States: yes, no, conditional (allowed with limits), unknown (not stated on the official pages we checked). Key rules checked by hand on 3 Nov 2026 on Kannur Airport's BCAS-based list and Akasa Air's conditions of carriage. Re-check every 3 months. 10 Nov 2026: items with 'rechecked' were checked again on IndiGo's and Air India's official lists and Akasa Air's conditions of carriage; 'cabin_short' and 'checked_short' are the direct answers on that item's own page (content/carry/*.md).
key_rules: Power banks go only in your cabin bag. Keep them with you, not in the overhead bin, and don't use or charge them during the flight.
Liquids in your cabin bag: each container 100 ml or less, all in one clear, resealable 1-litre bag. This applies on domestic flights too.
Dry coconut (copra), camphor, lighters, matches, e-cigarettes and firecrackers are banned in both cabin and check-in baggage.
Knives, scissors, tools, cricket bats and spice powders can't go in your cabin bag.
One power bank model, the MOBIKINS MK-PB-04, is banned on flights in any bag. Akasa Air's rules list it by name.

items.rule: Cabin bag only. Keep it in the seat pocket, under the seat or on you, never in the overhead bin. You can't use or charge it during the flight. Akasa Air and Air India allow up to 2 power banks or spare batteries, each up to 100 Wh. IndiGo needs the rating printed on it and refuses any over 160 Wh.
items.cabin_short: Up to 2 power banks of 100 Wh or less on Akasa Air and Air India. Keep it with you, not in the overhead bin, and don't use it on board.
items.checked_short: IndiGo, Air India and Akasa Air all ban power banks in check-in bags, even switched off.

items.rule: This model is banned on flights in any bag, and can't be sent as cargo either.

Take it out of your bag at security. Batteries over 100 Wh need airline approval. Keep it in your cabin bag: Akasa Air allows it in check-in only if fully switched off and protected, and SpiceJet says not to pack computers in check-in.
Allowed in the cabin. If you pack one in check-in, it must be fully switched off and protected from turning on.
Cabin bag only, each one protected from short circuits (in its pack or a pouch), never in the overhead bin. Akasa Air allows up to 2, each up to 100 Wh.
A trimmer with a built-in battery is fine in the cabin. In check-in it must be fully switched off and protected from turning on. IndiGo's list puts a trimmer without a battery in check-in only.
items.cabin_short: Yes, if it has a built-in battery. IndiGo's list says a trimmer without a battery goes in check-in only.
items.checked_short: Yes, switched fully off and protected so it can't turn on in the bag.

items.item: Smart bag with a fixed battery
items.rule: A smart bag whose battery can't be removed isn't allowed in the cabin or check-in (SpiceJet).
Lithium-battery personal vehicles such as hoverboards and self-balancing wheels aren't accepted in any baggage (FLY91).
Banned in both cabin and check-in baggage.
Air India Express doesn't allow drones in any baggage. Check with your airline before you fly with one.
Cabin bag: each container 100 ml or less, all in one clear, resealable bag of up to 1 litre, shown separately at security. Anything bigger goes in check-in.

Cabin bag: bottles of 100 ml or less inside the 1-litre clear bag, but IndiGo's list doesn't allow perfume or deo in the cabin at all. Check-in: up to 2 litres or 2 kg of toiletries in total, with no bottle over 500 ml (IndiGo, Air India, SpiceJet).
items.cabin_short: Only small bottles: 100 ml or less, inside your clear 1-litre liquids bag. Not on IndiGo, whose list doesn't allow perfume in the cabin.
items.checked_short: Yes. Up to 2 litres or 2 kg of perfume and toiletries in total, and no single bottle over 500 ml.

items.rule: Sprays follow the liquids rule in the cabin: 100 ml or less, inside the 1-litre clear bag. IndiGo's list doesn't allow deo in the cabin. Check-in: within the 2-litre toiletries limit, up to 500 ml per can, with the cap on.
Akasa Air allows hand sanitiser up to 350 ml in the cabin, inside the 1-litre clear bag.
A safety razor with the blades in a cartridge is fine in the cabin. Loose razor blades are banned in the cabin, so pack them in check-in.
Up to 100 ml in the cabin and up to 5 litres in check-in, in a sealed, leak-proof container (Akasa Air).
Keep the medicines you need in your cabin bag. Liquid medicines and inhalers over 100 ml are allowed with a prescription. IndiGo accepts medicines in check-in only with a prescription.
items.cabin_short: Keep the medicines you need with you. Liquid medicines over 100 ml are allowed if you need them on the journey and carry the prescription.
items.checked_short: Yes, with a prescription on IndiGo. Akasa Air advises not to put medicines in check-in, because a bag can be late or lost.

items.rule: Allowed in the cabin above 100 ml when you carry the prescription. Expect a check at security for needles.
Baby food for the journey is allowed in the cabin above 100 ml. SpiceJet lets you carry it on top of your cabin allowance.
Banned in both cabin and check-in baggage because it can catch fire.
Check-in: up to 5 litres or 5 kg (Air India, airport security list). Cabin bag: only in containers of 100 ml or less inside the 1-litre clear bag, and IndiGo doesn't allow ghee in the cabin at all.
items.cabin_short: Only a little: containers of 100 ml or less in your clear 1-litre bag. IndiGo doesn't allow ghee in the cabin at all.
items.checked_short: Yes. Up to 5 litres or 5 kg per person, packed so it can't leak.

items.rule: Check-in: allowed if packed so it can't leak or break (IndiGo, Air India). Cabin: IndiGo doesn't allow pickle, Air India doesn't allow chilli pickle, and oily pickle follows the 100 ml liquids rule. Akasa Air doesn't allow oily or strong-smelling food on board.

Dry sweets, snacks and biscuits are fine in both bags (IndiGo). Oily, messy or strong-smelling food isn't allowed on board (Akasa Air), and IndiGo doesn't take oily food in either bag. In check-in, pack food so it can't leak.
items.cabin_short: Yes for dry sweets, snacks and biscuits. No oily, messy or strong-smelling food, and sweets in syrup count as liquid.
items.checked_short: Yes for dry sweets and food packed so it can't leak. IndiGo doesn't accept oily food, even in check-in.

items.rule: All spices, powder or whole, including chilli, are banned in the cabin. Pack them in check-in.
Banned in the cabin, except round-bladed butter knives and plastic cutlery. Airlines may accept knives in check-in (SpiceJet).
Not allowed in the cabin. Airlines may accept them in check-in.
Allowed on domestic flights only, with a blade up to 15.24 cm (6 inches) and total length up to 22.86 cm (9 inches) (SpiceJet).
Banned in the cabin, except tiny screwdrivers in spectacle repair kits. Airlines may accept tools in check-in.
Realistic toy or replica guns are banned in the cabin. SpiceJet may accept them in check-in.
Cricket bats, hockey sticks, golf clubs and similar items are banned in the cabin. In check-in they go as special baggage, and SpiceJet charges a handling fee.

Folding umbrellas and umbrellas with a blunt tip can go in the cabin after the security check. An umbrella with a sharp tip goes in check-in (IndiGo, Air India). SpiceJet lets you carry one on top of your cabin allowance, and Akasa Air a compact folding one.
items.cabin_short: Yes for a folding umbrella or one with a blunt tip. An umbrella with a sharp tip must go in check-in.
items.checked_short: Any umbrella, including a long one with a sharp tip.

items.rule: Allowed in the cabin on top of your cabin allowance, after a security check (SpiceJet).
Banned in both cabin and check-in baggage.
Banned in both cabin and check-in baggage on Kannur Airport's list. One SpiceJet page says matches may be carried on you, so ask your airline.
Banned in both cabin and check-in baggage.
Fireworks, crackers and party poppers are banned in both cabin and check-in baggage.
Gas cylinders such as camping gas and butane, and used camping stoves, aren't accepted in any baggage (SpiceJet).

On domestic flights, pack it in check-in: up to 5 litres per person of drinks with 24–70% alcohol, in retail packaging (IndiGo, Air India, SpiceJet). Akasa Air also takes drinks of 24% or less in retail packaging. You can't drink it on board or take it to or from dry states such as Bihar and Gujarat.
items.cabin_short: Not alcohol from outside the airport. Alcohol you buy after security can go in the cabin, sealed in the shop's bag.
items.checked_short: Yes. Up to 5 litres per person of 24–70% alcohol, in its shop packing. Nothing over 70%.

items.rule: Alcohol bought after security can go in the cabin in its sealed bag; keep it sealed and keep the receipt. If you change from an international to a domestic flight in India, move it to check-in.
Keep them in your cabin bag: SpiceJet says not to put money, jewellery or precious metals in check-in, and Akasa Air doesn't cover them if lost.

faq.q: Can I carry a power bank on a flight in India?
faq.a: Yes, but only in your cabin bag, never in check-in. Keep it with you, not in the overhead bin, and don't use or charge it during the flight. Akasa Air allows up to 2, each up to 100 Wh.

faq.q: Is the 100 ml liquid rule only for international flights?
faq.a: No. In your cabin bag, each liquid, gel or cream must be 100 ml or less, all in one clear 1-litre bag, on domestic flights too. Bigger bottles go in check-in.

faq.q: Can I carry dry coconut on a flight?
faq.a: No. Dry coconut (copra) is banned in both cabin and check-in baggage because it can catch fire.

faq.q: Can I carry ghee on a flight?
faq.a: In check-in, up to 5 litres or 5 kg is allowed. In your cabin bag, only in containers of 100 ml or less inside the clear 1-litre bag, and IndiGo doesn't allow ghee in the cabin at all.

faq.q: Can I carry perfume in my cabin bag?
faq.a: On most airlines, yes, if each bottle is 100 ml or less and fits in your clear 1-litre liquids bag. IndiGo's list doesn't allow perfume or deo in the cabin, so on IndiGo pack it in check-in.

faq.q: Can I carry a razor on a flight?
faq.a: A safety razor with the blades in a cartridge is fine in your cabin bag. Loose razor blades must go in check-in.

faq.q: Can I carry alcohol on a domestic flight?
faq.a: In check-in only, up to 5 litres per person of 24–70% alcohol in retail packaging (IndiGo, Air India, SpiceJet), and not to or from dry states. Sealed duty-free alcohol can go in the cabin.

faq.q: Can I carry medicines on a flight?
faq.a: Yes. Keep them in your cabin bag. Liquid medicines and inhalers over 100 ml are allowed with a prescription.
